name: Wireflow
tagline: Node canvas for chaining image, video, and audio models into a pipeline you can re-run

pricing.notes: Starter is $24/mo monthly or $19.20/mo billed annually, and includes 1,600 credits. A free tier builds up to 5 workflows but cannot generate · generation is credit-gated on every plan.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 5 workflows; the first generation after setup is free, then generations consume paid credits.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1,600 credits per month; approximately 53 images or 94 video seconds; unlimited workflows.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 4,300 credits per month; approximately 143 images or 252 video seconds; unlimited workflows.
tiers.notes: Unused credits can roll over for up to 3 months; top-up is $10 for 600 credits.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 4 seats and 21,500 credits per month; approximately 716 images or 1,264 video seconds; unlimited workflows.
tiers.notes: Unused credits can roll over for up to 3 months; additional seats automatically change the bill at an unpublished rate.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats, credits and support; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 5 workflows; 1 first generation after setup is free, with no recurring included-credit allowance published.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Starter credits expire at each billing-period end; Professional and Team credits roll over only 3 months; credit top-ups cost $10, and extra Team-seat pricing is not published.

verdictSummary: Chaining a few model calls is a script, and ComfyUI already gives you a free node canvas. What you will not get in a weekend is the part after generation: a track and keyframe timeline with hosted rendering, and live multiplayer inside it. The graph is vibecodable. The editor attached to it is not.
coreLoopDIY: Wire model calls into a graph on a canvas, hit run, then layer and time the generated pieces into a finished cut.
requirements: fal.ai API key or another hosted model provider
somewhere to run it that stays up while jobs finish
a GPU only if you self-host the models instead
whatYouLose: a compositor and keyframe timeline, with hosted rendering
live multiplayer on the canvas and inside the editor
hundreds of model schemas kept current for you
paid steps that never fire by accident, and jobs that survive a closed tab
a library of ready-made pipelines to fork, and boards you can share
moatNotes: collaborative editor depth and execution reliability
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody vibecodes a keyframe timeline in a weekend. And the DIY failure mode is not that it breaks, it is that it keeps running while double-charging a call that 404'd or losing a render you already paid for.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.desc: The node canvas under half the AI-media industry, minus the credits and plus the cable spaghetti.

facts.install: Windows or macOS desktop installer, Windows portable archive, or manual Python install on Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.engines: Local and downloadable image, video, audio, 3D, and text models including Stable Diffusion/SDXL/SD3.5, FLUX, Wan, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, and Mochi; optional API nodes connect to hosted providers
facts.dataFormat: Models, inputs, outputs, and workflow JSON live in the local ComfyUI data tree; generated media can embed workflow and seed metadata, while API nodes transmit selected inputs to their provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the deeper workflow engine, but lacks Wireflow's managed providers, cloud compute, collaboration, and polished project sharing.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU, enough VRAM and disk for multi-gigabyte models, and a working model/workflow must be chosen before useful output appears

alternatives.name: NodeTool
alternatives.desc: A creative node canvas for image, video and audio with a timeline; 450 stars, but active releases and real installers.

facts.install: Install the macOS .dmg, signed Windows .exe, or Linux AppImage; Docker Compose is available for self-hosting
facts.engines: Local Ollama, llama.cpp/GGUF, MLX, Nunchaku, Hugging Face, and diffusion/media models, plus BYOK providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, FAL, Replicate, KIE, ElevenLabs, and Hugging Face
facts.dataFormat: Workflows, projects, assets, files, provider settings, and vector indexes live locally in YAML, SQLite/SQLite-vec, and application storage; optional S3 or Supabase storage is supported, and cloud nodes transmit their inputs
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the closest functional match, but users must operate the compute and provider keys themselves and team collaboration is less mature.
facts.setupBlocker: No useful model or provider is bundled: the user must add an API key or download a multi-gigabyte local model, and some local backends add a large Python/Conda environment

alternatives.name: SwarmUI
alternatives.desc: A reusable image-video-audio workflow graph with a simpler Generate tab for days when the wires can wait.

facts.install: Run the Windows installer script, the Linux launch script, or install .NET/Python/Homebrew prerequisites and run launch-macos.sh on macOS; Docker is optional
facts.engines: Uses ComfyUI as its main backend for Stable Diffusion, SDXL, FLUX, Wan, LTX, MiniMax, ACE-Step, and other image/video/audio workflows; an Automatic1111-compatible backend is optional
facts.dataFormat: Configuration, users, models, workflows, generated media, and history live in the local SwarmUI installation and configured model/output directories
facts.gapVsPaid: Its graph is capable, but the product is image-generation-first and thinner for audio, timeline work, collaboration, and managed re-runs.
facts.setupBlocker: The backend and models still have to be downloaded, and non-Windows installs require command-line prerequisites such as .NET, Python, and Git

notes: The graph is a weekend. The editor and the multiplayer are not · try ComfyUI first, and know that credits carry a margin over what the models cost at the provider.
prompt:
Build me a local visual pipeline runner for AI media generation. Requirements:

- One Vite + React app and one Express server in the same repo, SQLite via
  better-sqlite3, no auth, no accounts, runs on localhost.
- Canvas on React Flow: drag nodes from a palette, wire outputs to inputs,
  pan and zoom, autosave the graph to SQLite on every change.
- Six node types only: Text input, Image import (upload to ./storage), Prompt
  template (interpolates {{upstream}} values), Image generate, Video generate,
  Preview. Generate nodes call fal.ai through @fal-ai/client, FAL_KEY in .env.
- Model config lives in models.json: per model, its fal path and which fields
  are wired ports versus typed-in settings. Ship exactly two entries,
  fal-ai/flux/dev and fal-ai/kling-video/v1/standard/text-to-video.
- Run = topological sort, execute layer by layer, store each node's output in
  SQLite keyed by node id plus a hash of its resolved inputs. Re-running only
  re-executes nodes whose input hash changed.
- Generate nodes NEVER run on edit. Only the Run button or a per-node run
  button submits a job. This rule is the whole point, do not add reactive
  auto-execution anywhere.
- Submit through fal's queue API and poll by request id, persisting the request
  id BEFORE the first poll, so a finished job survives a server restart.
- README covers where FAL_KEY goes, that every run spends real money at
  fal.ai, and how to add a third model to models.json.

Excluded on purpose: multiplayer, credits and billing, iterators or fan-out
over arrays, video assembly, hosted deploys, and any provider besides fal.ai.
